title: Business SOX Compliance Manager
description: Who we are Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale. Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term. About the role: Samsara is looking for an experienced manager to lead SOX business process compliance and help keep the trust in our financial reporting as strong as the business we’re building. As part of our SOX Compliance team, you’ll help oversee and strengthen Samsara’s global control environment, protecting the accuracy of our financial reporting and keeping us compliant as we scale. You’ll partner closely with IT and business process owners to design and implement controls, spot gaps early, and drive remediation to the finish line. We’re looking for someone who takes real ownership. You bring deep, hands-on SOX expertise, a track record of delivering projects reliably, and the confidence to run with complex work independently. If you take pride in being the person others count on to get it done right, we’d love to meet you. This is a remote position open to candidates based in the US  except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area. You should apply if: You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely. You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment. You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers. You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.  In this role, you will:   Develop, lead, and execute periodic financial risk assessments, materiality calculations, and scoping of the SOX program Develop and deliver training to SOX control owners, including process documentation, testing methodology, management review controls, and controls over Information Produced by the Entity (IPE). Conduct walkthroughs across all business process areas and work with business process owners to ensure timely review and updates to the control documentation Collaborate cross functionally to design leading edge practices with a financial compliance mindset across several complex business process areas. Help drive the SOX AI transformation strategy by identifying high-value opportunities, implementing AI-enabled solutions, and driving adoption and new ways of working across the global SOX organization. title: Senior Director, Cybersecurity and AI Risk Oversight
description: Playing an essential role in the U.S. economy, Fannie Mae is foundational to housing finance. Here, your expertise can help fuel purpose-driven innovation that expands access to homeownership and affordable rental housing across the country. Join Fannie Mae to grow your career and help people find a place to call home. Job Description The Senior Director, Cybersecurity Risk Oversight Lead is responsible for advancing the Chief Risk and Compliance Division's (CRCD) independent cybersecurity risk oversight strategy. This role serves as a senior second line of defense (2LOD) leader responsible for overseeing cybersecurity risk governance, risk identification and assessment, risk appetite, issue management, emerging risk monitoring, regulatory engagement, and executive reporting. Serving as a strategic partner to enterprise leadership, technology teams, and control functions, this role provides independent oversight and credible challenge to ensure cybersecurity risks are effectively identified, measured, monitored, managed, and reported. The position provides transparency into the firm's cybersecurity risk posture, control effectiveness, remediation progress, and emerging threats while supporting informed decision-making by executive management, risk committees, and regulators. The role also oversees cybersecurity risks associated with emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, frontier models, agentic systems, and quantum computing, ensuring risks are appropriately governed and aligned with enterprise risk appetite. THE IMPACT YOU WILL MAKE Cybersecurity Risk Oversight & Governance Lead independent oversight and credible challenge of the enterprise cybersecurity risk management program. Assess the effectiveness of cybersecurity governance, risk management practices, and control environments. Provide independent review and challenge of cybersecurity strategies, risk assessments, exceptions, risk acceptances, and remediation plans. Evaluate cybersecurity risk exposures against approved risk appetite statements, limits, and thresholds. Identify material risk concentrations, systemic control weaknesses, and emerging risk trends. Promote accountability, transparency, and effective risk management across the enterprise. Cyber Risk Assessment, Monitoring & Reporting Oversee the assessment, aggregation, monitoring, and reporting of cybersecurity risks across the enterprise. Establish and maintain cybersecurity risk metrics, key risk indicators (KRIs), and risk appetite measures. Monitor cybersecurity events, control deficiencies, audit findings, and issue remediation activities. Develop executive-level dashboards, scorecards, and risk reporting for senior leadership, risk committees, and the Board. Translate complex cybersecurity risks into clear business impacts and actionable recommendations. Emerging Technology & Cybersecurity Risk Oversight Provide independent oversight of cybersecurity risks associated with artificial intelligence, frontier models, autonomous agents, and other emerging technologies. Assess risks related to AI-enabled cyber threats, adversarial attacks, model compromise, data exposure, and AI supply-chain vulnerabilities. Evaluate cybersecurity implications of advanced AI capabilities and emerging technology adoption across the enterprise. Lead oversight of enterprise preparedness for quantum computing threats and post-quantum cryptography transition efforts. Monitor emerging cyber threats, technology developments, and regulatory expectations to identify risks that may impact the firm's security posture. Issue Management, Regulatory Engagement & Assurance Provide oversight of cybersecurity issues, corrective action plans, risk acceptances, and remediation activities. Review and challenge issue severity, root cause analysis, remediation effectiveness, and closure decisions. Support cybersecurity regulatory examinations, findings remediation, and supervisory commitments. Partner with Internal Audit, Compliance, and other assurance functions to assess cybersecurity risk management effectiveness. Escalate material cybersecurity risks, control concerns, and adverse trends through established governance channels. Executive Leadership & Stakeholder Management Serve as a trusted cybersecurity risk advisor to executive leadership and governance committees. Build strong partnerships across technology, business, risk, audit, compliance, and regulatory stakeholders. Develop board level presentations and present cybersecurity risk perspectives and recommendations to senior leadership and Executive-level forums. Lead and develop a high-performing team of cybersecurity risk professionals. Foster a culture of accountability, transparency, continuous improvement, and sound risk management. title: Senior Manager, Accounts Payable - Payments
description: About the Team OpenAI’s Procurement team makes working with the world easy, fast, and safe. We connect supplier readiness, purchasing, invoicing, and payment so teams can move with confidence as OpenAI scales. Accounts Payable provides the trusted data, dependable execution, and financial discipline behind that experience. About the Role We’re looking for an Accounts Payable Senior Manager to own and scale supplier payment operations. You’ll be responsible for accurate, timely payments, strong controls, and dependable service as OpenAI grows. This is a hands-on leadership role. You’ll review and approve supplier payment runs, oversee work initiated by our BPO teams and AP agents, as well as personally resolve complex exceptions. You’ll stay close to execution during volume spikes and month-end close while building the processes, coverage, and systems the team needs to scale. You’ll partner with Procurement, Supplier Master Data Operations, Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Finance Systems, and existing AP processing teams to make payments reliable from payment readiness through settlement reconciliation. You’ll clarify handoffs, address recurring failures, and improve ERP, banking, and procurement workflows. You’ll also apply automation and AI where they improve accuracy, service, or team capacity, with appropriate controls and human review. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office (Mon-Wed) per week and we offer relocation assistance to new employees. We’re looking for someone with: - Strategic AP leadership and a hands-on approach to scaling systems and processes, with strong attention to detail. - Demonstrated ownership of complex indirect AP and supplier-payment operations, including PO and non-PO workflows. - Experience leading teams or outsourced delivery partners, setting expectations, developing capability, and managing performance. - Strong payment-control judgment and experience investigating duplicates, bank-detail changes, and payment failures. - Working depth in AP accounting, reconciliations, accrual inputs, and close coordination. - Experience translating AP needs into ERP or procurement-system improvements with measurable results. - Clear communication and the ability to influence partners and senior stakeholders in ambiguous situations. In this role, you will: - Own supplier payment operations: Review and approve payment runs for supplier and payment data accuracy, required approvals, and exception resolution. Oversee manual disbursements and payment inquiries within established authority and segregation-of-duties requirements. - Resolve complex exceptions: Act as the primary escalation point for payment holds, rejected or returned payments, potential duplicates, and close blockers. Work with Treasury, banking partners, Accounting, and AP processing teams to establish the status, resolve the cause, and verify the outcome before retrying or closing an issue. - Strengthen payment readiness: Partner with Procurement and existing AP teams to resolve invoice, PO, approval, and supplier-data gaps that affect payment. Establish clear owners and follow through on recurring upstream issues. - Support forecasting and close: Provide reliable payment forecasts and cash-needs inputs to Treasury. Reconcile payment activity and exceptions, including payments after AP close, so Accounting has the evidence it needs for close and cutoff decisions. - Maintain effective controls: Uphold SOX-aligned approvals, independent supplier bank-detail verification, segregation of duties, and audit-ready documentation. Support internal and external audits and remediate control gaps with the relevant owners. - Improve systems and processes: Define payment workflow and reporting requirements with Finance Systems and other partners. Test ERP and bank integrations, including host-to-host workflows, and introduce automation or AI with validated outputs, exception handling, and clear accountability. - Lead BPO delivery and capacity: Set clear SLAs and KPIs, review quality and performance, coach service partners, and maintain documented procedures and backup coverage. Plan for volume spikes and close demands. - Report performance and risk: Own clear reporting on payment timeliness, exceptions, rejection and return trends, forecast accuracy, service quality, and control issues. Explain priorities and progress to stakeholders and leadership. You might thrive in this role if you: - Bring 8+ years in AP, payments, or related finance operations, or equivalent experience, with personal ownership of complex supplier-payment operations and material exceptions. - Have worked across indirect supplier spend in a high-growth or scaling environment, balancing immediate delivery with durable process improvements. - Understand how invoices, approvals, supplier records, payment instructions, bank status, settlement, and reconciliation fit together, and can investigate discrepancies across them. - Bri

title: Technical Accounting/SEC Reporting Lead
description: Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. Lambda's mission is to make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone the power of superintelligence. One person, one GPU. If you'd like to build the world's best AI cloud, join us. *Note: This position requires presence in our San Jose office location 4 days per week; Lambda’s designated work from home day is currently Tuesday. What You’ll Do - Lead technical accounting research and prepare memos for complex, non-routine transactions in accordance with U.S. GAAP - Analyze accounting implications of significant transactions, including revenue, equity, debt, business combinations, leases, and stock-based compensation - Partner cross-functionally (Legal, Tax, FP&A, Treasury) to assess accounting impacts and provide guidance ahead of execution - Develop and maintain accounting policies; evaluate and implement new FASB and SEC guidance in preparation for public company readiness - Support IPO readiness efforts, including drafting technical disclosures, assisting with S-1/10-K preparation, and enhancing financial statement presentation - Assist with consolidated financial statement preparation, footnotes, and reporting package reviews to ensure accuracy and SEC compliance - Support external audits and SOX readiness by preparing documentation, strengthening controls, and improving close and reporting processes - Contribute to M&A, system implementations, and other strategic initiatives to support company growth What we look for in you: - Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field - 4+ years of experience in technical accounting, preferably within a Big 4 firm and/or a publicly traded company - Active CPA required - Strong knowledge of the U.S. GAAP with experience analyzing complex and non-routine transactions (e.g., revenue recognition, leases, equity, debt, business combinations) - Proven ability to research accounting guidance and prepare clear, well-supported technical accounting memos - Understanding of SEC reporting and disclosure requirements - Experience partnering cross-functionally to assess accounting implications of business initiatives - Familiarity with ERP and reporting tools (e.g., NetSuite, Workiva) - Advanced Excel skills and strong analytical capabilities - Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical guidance into practical recommendations - Detail-oriented, proactive, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment Nice to haves: - Big 4 audit or accounting advisory experience with strong technical accounting expertise - Deep knowledge of ASC 606 (revenue), ASC 842 (leases), and ASC 718 (stock-based compensation), including memo preparation and policy development - Experience with pre-IPO technical matters, including equity instruments, preferred stock, warrants, EPS, and SEC reporting considerations - Strong understanding of the U.S. GAAP financial reporting, including preparation and review of financial statements and footnote disclosures - Experience supporting IPO readiness, S-1/10-K preparation, and PCAOB audits - Background in high-growth, pre-IPO or public technology companies (SaaS/AI preferred) - Exposure to M&A and purchase accounting, particularly in revenue and equity-related areas - Demonstrated ability to strengthen controls and build scalable accounting processes in fast-paced environments Salary Range Information The annual salary range for this position has been set based on market data and other factors. However, a salary higher or lower than this range may be appropriate for a candidate whose qualifications differ meaningfully from those listed in the job description.
